title: Write git stdin from a thread so a long patch-id stream cannot deadlock
action: Fix found by the p15-1 slice judge, per pstack-0-15-port D2 (fail open on every git error — a hang is not fail-open). In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/git.rs, `run_git_stdin` (search `pub(crate) fn run_git_stdin`) calls `write_all` on the child's stdin BEFORE reading stdout. `git patch-id --stable` prints one line per commit while it reads, so past roughly 800 commits its 64 KiB stdout pipe fills, it stops reading, `write_all` blocks, and `bee worktree merge` hangs. Change it so the write and the read cannot block each other: take the child's stdin, move the input into a `std::thread::spawn` that does the `write_all` and drops the handle, then call `wait_with_output` on the child; join the thread after (ignore its result — a broken pipe on the write side is the child exiting early, which the exit status already reports). Keep the return shape and every fail-open path exactly as they are. Also fix the typo in docs/knowledge/areas/worktree-parallelism/returning-and-the-merge-gate.md: the bullet heading `A cleaner rebase is not stale proof` reads `A clean rebase is not stale proof`. No new test is required by this cell: the existing rebase and stale tests pin the behavior; the deadlock needs an 800-commit fixture that is not worth its runtime. No code comments (comment ratchet `bee dev comment-baseline --check`).
verify: `PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee verbs::worktree::tests` is green. `rg -n 'A clean rebase is not stale proof' docs/knowledge/areas/worktree-parallelism/returning-and-the-merge-gate.md` returns one line. `.bee/bin/bee dev comment-baseline --check` is clean.

truths: run_git_stdin never blocks on a full stdout pipe
every existing worktree test stays green

artifacts.substantive: stdin written from a spawned thread, stdout read with wait_with_output

prohibitions: No change to the GitOut shape
